title: QC, preprocessing, and graph clustering of two human bone-marrow samples

sources.locator: Sections Quality Control through Clustering; setup and sample loading cells

scientific_use: Combine two filtered gene-expression matrices from healthy human bone marrow donors, calculate QC metrics, remove low-detection cells/genes, call doublets with Scrublet per sample, normalize and log-transform counts, select highly variable genes by sample, compute PCA and a neighbor graph, embed with UMAP, and identify graph communities with Leiden. This yields a processed AnnData with QC annotations, doublet scores, feature selection, low-dimensional representations, and cluster labels.
tool_role_basis: The notebook applies documented Scanpy APIs (sc.pp.calculate_qc_metrics, filter_cells/filter_genes, scrublet, normalize_total, log1p, highly_variable_genes, tl.pca, pp.neighbors, tl.umap, tl.leiden) to observed expression data; it does not implement those algorithms.

inputs.meaning: Two filtered 10x Genomics gene-expression count matrices, sample IDs s1d1 and s1d3; tutorial describes approximately 8,000 cells per sample and 36,601 measured genes.
inputs.format: 10x HDF5 feature-barcode matrix files s1d1_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 and s1d3_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5, read into AnnData and concatenated with sample labels.
inputs.processing_stage: filtered_feature_bc_matrix; before tutorial QC and downstream transforms

outputs.meaning: AnnData containing QC metrics, sample-aware doublet predictions and scores, retained count layer, normalized/log1p matrix, HVG annotations, PCA, neighbor graph, UMAP, and Leiden cluster labels; QC and embedding plots are also produced.
outputs.format: AnnData in memory; tutorial illustrates saving plots but specifies no required output file.

dependencies: Python, Scanpy, AnnData, pooch; the notebook's source environment is not a task specification.
Scrublet implementation is invoked through Scanpy; data retrieval uses the Figshare DOI registry.
The clustering section relies on the neighbor graph produced upstream; manual thresholds and sample metadata are part of the workflow.

evidence.locator: Intro and sample-loading cells; Quality Control, Doublet detection, Normalization, Feature selection, Dimensionality Reduction, Nearest neighbor graph construction and visualization, and Clustering headings/code cells

limitations: Tutorial notes permissive filtering thresholds and recommends revisiting QC; expert review is needed for biological suitability.
No execution was performed in this inventory task. Runtime, deterministic cluster labels, and output grading are unverified.
Notebook has later manual annotation and marker analysis covered in the related unit; no fixed task output contract is specified.

title: Marker-guided cell annotation and cluster differential expression in bone marrow

sources.locator: Sections Manual cell-type annotation, Marker gene set, and Differentially-expressed Genes as Markers

scientific_use: Compare marker-gene expression across Leiden resolutions with dotplots, assign broad lineage labels to a coarse clustering, compute cluster-versus-rest marker genes using Wilcoxon rank tests, and inspect gene rankings and expression to support cell identity interpretation. Useful outputs are cluster annotation fields and ranked marker tables/plots.
tool_role_basis: The notebook uses Scanpy Leiden, plotting, rank_genes_groups, and rank_genes_groups_df APIs and a cited external marker set; it does not create a new statistical method.

inputs.meaning: The AnnData and neighbor graph from the preceding QC/clustering workflow, plus a notebook-defined set of marker genes for expected marrow lineages.
inputs.format: AnnData with sample, expression matrix, PCA/neighbors, UMAP, and cluster labels; Python mapping from lineage names to gene symbols.

outputs.meaning: Multiple Leiden resolutions, broad manually assigned cell_type_lvl1 labels, marker expression dotplots, cluster-specific differential-expression rankings and selected-gene UMAPs.
outputs.format: AnnData obs/uns annotations and ranking results; plots; gene tables retrievable with scanpy.get.rank_genes_groups_df.

dependencies: Requires the upstream unit's AnnData, neighbor graph and Leiden result.
Marker list is notebook content adapted from Single Cell Best Practices annotation chapter; manual interpretation is required.

Wilcoxon statistics assume cells as independent samples in the shown analysis; tutorial explicitly cautions about very small p-values and suggests sample-level pseudobulk followed by PyDESeq2 for a more conservative alternative.

evidence.locator: Manual cell-type annotation through Differentially-expressed Genes as Markers; code calls leiden at resolutions 0.02, 0.5, 2.0, dotplot, rank_genes_groups(method="wilcoxon"), and get.rank_genes_groups_df

limitations: Cell labels shown are tutorial judgments and require biological validation; not a gold-standard annotation set.
Marker symbols and annotations may need species/build alignment checks before reuse.
Tutorial warns cell-level differential expression can inflate significance; task author should decide whether to use its shown analysis or sample-aware pseudobulk.
No execution or grader validation was performed.

title: PAGA lineage graph and diffusion pseudotime for mouse myeloid progenitors

sources.locator: Preprocessing and Visualization; Optional: Denoising the graph; Clustering and PAGA; Recomputing the embedding using PAGA-initialization; Reconstructing gene changes along PAGA paths

scientific_use: Apply a Zheng-style preprocessing recipe and PCA to the Paul et al. mouse progenitor expression data, build and optionally denoise a neighbor graph, cluster cells, annotate clusters using lineage markers, compute PAGA connectivity between annotated clusters, initialize a graph embedding from PAGA, choose a stem-cell root for diffusion pseudotime, and visualize expression changes along erythroid, neutrophil, and monocyte paths. Potential artifacts include cluster labels, abstract lineage graph, pseudotime, and gene-expression summaries along paths.
tool_role_basis: The workflow composes Scanpy recipe, PCA, neighbors, Louvain, PAGA, graph embedding, and DPT APIs on a supplied dataset; it contains marker-based interpretations but no implementation of these algorithms.

inputs.meaning: Non-logarithmized mouse myeloid progenitor expression with 2,730 cells and 3,451 genes after loader adaptation; source-observed cluster IDs and root metadata are provided by loader.
inputs.format: AnnData from scanpy.datasets.paul15(); backed by HDF5 with expression, gene names, cell names, cluster IDs, and informative gene names.

outputs.meaning: Annotated cluster partition, PAGA abstraction graph, graph layout initialized from PAGA, diffusion pseudotime from selected stem-cell root, and average expression profiles for selected genes along three lineage paths.
outputs.format: AnnData obs/uns/obsm outputs, plots, and CSV files written by the example for path summaries.
outputs.processing_stage: trajectory reconstruction and lineage gene-change summaries

dependencies: Requires Scanpy/AnnData, graph/clustering dependencies, and Paul15 expression data.
Optional denoising uses diffusion-map coordinates to rebuild neighbors; the tutorial explicitly says this step is not required.
The tutorial uses Louvain to reproduce the historical paper analysis and notes Leiden would be used today.
Marker-gene labels and the selected lineage paths are supplied as biological interpretation; exact path indices depend on category ordering.

evidence.locator: Title and analysis sections listed above; calls recipe_zheng17, pca, neighbors, diffmap, louvain, paga, draw_graph(init_pos="paga"), dpt, and paga_path
paul15() docstring and body: raw-data statement, 2730 x 3451 example, HDF5 arrays and annotation construction

limitations: Loader states data were emailed by the Amit Lab and points to an R loader; current underlying study data location and redistribution terms are not established.
Source comments refer to 3,461 informative genes while documented AnnData shape is 3,451; inspect exact array contents if gene count matters.
This is pseudotime and graph inference, not measured temporal lineage tracing; direction depends on selected root and cluster paths.
The optional denoising path and exact numerical stability were not executed or validated here.

title: Reference-based cell-label mapping and BBKNN batch integration

sources.locator: Sections PBMCs and Mapping PBMCs using ingest; Pancreas, BBKNN, Mapping onto a reference batch using ingest, Evaluating consistency, and Visualizing distributions across batches

scientific_use: Compare asymmetric PCA/neighbor/UMAP reference mapping with BBKNN graph integration. On PBMC data, map cluster labels and embeddings from a processed reference to a reduced query. On four-study human pancreas data, inspect batch effects, apply BBKNN or map batches iteratively from one reference, compare mapped labels against original annotations with confusion tables, and visualize batch distribution. Supports tasks about preserving reference structure, integration tradeoffs, and identifying annotation inconsistencies.
tool_role_basis: Notebook applies Scanpy tl.ingest, external.pp.bbknn, PCA, neighbors, UMAP, embedding_density and pandas contingency summaries; method implementations are external/delegated library calls, not authored here.

inputs.meaning: Alternative PBMC example: annotated pbmc3k processed reference and pbmc68k reduced query, intersected on common variables before mapping.
inputs.format: AnnData objects loaded from Scanpy dataset functions; shared gene axis required.

inputs.meaning: Human pancreas expression dataset from four cited studies with batch and celltype annotations, stored as a pre-intersected-gene AnnData file; notebook removes five minority cell classes for one visualization path.
inputs.format: H5AD at data/pancreas.h5ad; backup URL is provided in the read call.
inputs.processing_stage: curated/integrated multi-study input before tutorial integration

outputs.meaning: Mapped labels and embeddings, batch-integrated neighbor graph and UMAP, batch density visualization, and crosstabs comparing mapped and original cell type labels.
outputs.format: AnnData obs/obsm/obsp/uns outputs, plots, pandas contingency tables.

dependencies: Scanpy, AnnData, pandas; BBKNN method is imported from external integration package.
Ingest uses annotated reference PCA and neighbor/UMAP state and requires common variables with queries.
Reference composition constrains mapping: tutorial specifically cautions that a small reference may omit biological variation and clusters.
Pancreas portion uses the given batch and celltype metadata; reference batch is selected as batch '0'.

evidence.locator: Intro describes ingest model and contrasts BBKNN; PBMC mapping cells; Pancreas data and BBKNN/ingest workflows; Evaluating consistency crosstabs; embedding_density

limitations: PBMC example uses Scanpy's preprocessed/reduced assets; complete provenance and relation to underlying source observations need data-loader review.
Pancreas H5AD size, license, precise curation pipeline and detailed per-study sample design are not established here.
Tutorial's cell-type comparisons expose ambiguous/inconsistent labels; original labels are not a gold standard.
Integration, runtime, output stability and appropriate evaluation were not executed or validated.

title: Cell-cycle scoring and regression in mouse hematopoietic progenitors

sources.locator: Load data through final PCA projection sections

scientific_use: Load a Nestorowa mouse hematopoietic progenitor expression matrix, filter cells and genes, normalize and log-transform, score S and G2M phases from a curated gene list, regress both scores from the expression matrix, then compare PCA on cell-cycle genes before and after regression. Supports inspecting whether cell-cycle variation dominates embedding structure and how covariate regression changes it.
tool_role_basis: The notebook applies Scanpy scoring, preprocessing, regression, and PCA APIs; curated gene lists are read from supplied files, with no algorithm implemented in the tutorial.

inputs.meaning: Mouse hematopoietic progenitor expression matrix from the Nestorowa study, plus a human 97-gene S/G2M reference list whose genes are intersected with observed variables.
inputs.format: Tab-delimited matrix within a ZIP archive and separate text gene-list file.

inputs.meaning: Tirosh et al. cell-cycle gene symbols split into S and G2M phases; notebook filters genes absent from matrix.
inputs.format: Text list, 97 human gene symbols bundled in ZIP; ortholog compilation would be needed for alternate species.

outputs.meaning: AnnData phase annotations and S/G2M scores; PCA projections on cell-cycle genes before and after regressing scores.
outputs.format: AnnData obs fields and PCA coordinates/plots.

dependencies: Scanpy and AnnData; pooch downloads the ZIP.
Cell matrix is transposed on read; tutorial applies min_genes=200 and min_cells=3, normalize_total(target_sum=1e4), log1p before scoring.
PCA visualization uses a subset AnnData containing cell-cycle genes; original object remains the target of regress_out.
Reference list is human; source says alternate organisms require ortholog list compilation.

evidence.locator: Intro identifies Nestorowa progenitors and source archive; cells load matrix and Tirosh list, score_genes_cell_cycle, regress_out on S_score/G2M_score, and compare PCA before/after

limitations: Notebook calls the expression matrix a toy dataset; cells are from mouse but reference list is human, and no orthology transformation is shown.
The newer corrected Nestorowa URL is mentioned but the notebook uses the Dropbox benchmarking ZIP; their equivalence was not inspected.
No analysis was executed; score stability and suitability of regression are unverified.
